pr.title: Perform InstSimplify before ReferencePropagation.
pr.description:
`InstSimplify` clears CFG caches.

But it currently happens between `ReferencePropagation` and `GVN`, which both use dominators, a quite expensive computation.

processing.reason: PR 147483 is strictly a MIR pass-scheduling/performance change: it moves `instsimplify::InstSimplify::AfterSimplifyCfg` ahead of `ref_prop::ReferencePropagation` and `sroa::ScalarReplacementOfAggregates` so a CFG-cache-clearing pass no longer sits between two dominator-tree consumers (ReferencePropagation and GVN). It does not change any rewrite rule, and the historical order was still semantically correct—only suboptimal due to redundant dominator-tree recomputation. Both schedules produce semantically equivalent optimized MIR, so there is no source-grounded value-level counterexample to encode. Manufacturing one (e.g. an arbitrary expression or return-value change) would not be justified by the PR. Per the frozen analysis's own guidance, the appropriate validation is schedule equivalence and compile-time/dominator recomputation, which the test_program_pair value-difference harness cannot express.

analysis.summary: This merged PR reorders MIR optimization passes so that InstSimplify (which invalidates CFG caches) runs before ReferencePropagation/SROA rather than between ReferencePropagation and GVN. ReferencePropagation and GVN both consume the dominator tree, so the old order forced an expensive dominator-tree recomputation. The reusable lesson is a pass-scheduling invariant: do not insert a CFG-cache-invalidating pass between consecutive dominator-tree consumers.
analysis.originalLogic: The original pipeline scheduled, after inlining and CFG simplification: `&ref_prop::ReferencePropagation`, `&sroa::ScalarReplacementOfAggregates`, `&multiple_return_terminators::MultipleReturnTerminators`, then `&instsimplify::InstSimplify::AfterSimplifyCfg`, `&simplify::SimplifyLocals::BeforeConstProp`, `&dead_store_elimination::DeadStoreElimination::Initial`, and finally `&gvn::GVN`. Thus InstSimplify sat between ReferencePropagation and GVN. The PR description states: "But it currently happens between `ReferencePropagation` and `GVN`, which both use dominators, a quite expensive computation."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically suboptimal scheduling placed the cache-clearing InstSimplify pass between ReferencePropagation and GVN (with SROA also before InstSimplify). Because InstSimplify "clears CFG caches" and both ReferencePropagation and GVN "use dominators", this ordering invalidated cached CFG/dominator data between two dominator consumers and forced redundant dominator-tree computation. The corrected ordering moves `instsimplify::InstSimplify::AfterSimplifyCfg` before `ref_prop::ReferencePropagation` and `sroa::ScalarReplacementOfAggregates`, keeping GVN after them. This is a pass-order/performance transformation, not a wrong program rewrite; do not invent a value-level miscompile for it.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies that reach rustc's optimization pipeline after inlining, storage-marker removal, unreachable-branch/enum handling, and SimplifyCfg, and that contain references/aggregates such that ReferencePropagation, SROA, and GVN all run. The relevant variation is the pass schedule: old order `ReferencePropagation -> SROA -> MultipleReturnTerminators -> InstSimplify -> SimplifyLocals -> DSE -> GVN` versus new order `InstSimplify -> ReferencePropagation -> SROA -> SimplifyLocals -> DSE -> GVN`, with MultipleReturnTerminators moved before InstSimplify. Two otherwise identical compilations differing only in this schedule exercise the optimization.
analysis.trigger: Scheduling `instsimplify::InstSimplify::AfterSimplifyCfg` immediately between `ref_prop::ReferencePropagation` and `gvn::GVN` in `run_optimization_passes`, where the cache-clearing InstSimplify invalidates the dominator tree used by both neighboring passes.
preconditions: The MIR optimization pipeline has run inlining and CFG simplification so that ReferencePropagation, SROA, and GVN are scheduled.
InstSimplify is placed after SimplifyCfg so it can discover peephole opportunities, but must not sit between dominator-tree consumers.
ReferencePropagation and GVN both rely on dominators, and InstSimplify clears CFG caches.
pitfalls: Do not treat this PR as a semantic bug fix: the patch only changes pass ordering and comments, and no executed reproduction or value-level miscompile was shown.
Keep InstSimplify after SimplifyCfg; the source comment says this ordering 'allows us to discover new opportunities for peephole optimizations.'

Do not insert another CFG-cache-invalidating pass between ReferencePropagation and GVN; the added comment explicitly says 'This invalidates CFG caches, so avoid putting between `ReferencePropagation` and `GVN` which both use the dominator tree.'
SROA is moved together with ReferencePropagation; preserve its position relative to the dominator-consuming chain rather than attaching this observation to unrelated passes.
analysis.testStrategy: Validate the schedule itself rather than expecting a new semantic regression test: compile representative MIR inputs with the old versus new pass order and check semantic equivalence of optimized MIR, plus measure compile time / dominator-tree recomputation. Confirm InstSimplify still follows SimplifyCfg and precedes ReferencePropagation/SROA, and that GVN remains after them with no cache-clearing pass in between. The supplied patch contains only `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/lib.rs` pipeline edits and no regression test changes; no compiler was built and no execution or reproduction is claimed.
